text: dsh-linalg 是一个面向 DSH agent 的线性代数工具插件，通过注册工具让 agent 执行矩阵和向量计算。它提供矩阵乘法、转置与行列式等运算，求解线性方程组并区分唯一解、无穷多解和无解，还支持 LU、QR、Cholesky 分解、对称矩阵特征分解、最小二乘以及向量点积、范数和投影。计算使用本地数值运算，输入为 JSON 数组；矩阵维度和结果精度可配置。适合需要在 DSH 会话中获得可复核数学计算结果的用户；源码未显示外部服务或密钥要求。

dsh-linalg gives DSH agents local matrix, linear-system, factorization, least-squares, and vector tools. It accepts JSON arrays and offers configurable matrix size and output precision. Useful for math calculations in DSH sessions; the source shows no external service or API key requirement.
想让 DSH 帮我计算矩阵的行列式、逆矩阵或秩。
有一组线性方程，能不能判断它是唯一解、无解还是有多个解？
I need a least-squares fit for an overdetermined system and its residual.
dsh-linalg 的功能「矩阵运算与分解」：DSH agent 可调用工具对 JSON 矩阵执行乘法、行列式、逆矩阵、秩等操作，也可计算 LU、QR 或 Cholesky 因子并返回分解残差。
dsh-linalg 的功能「线性系统与向量计算」：agent 提交系数矩阵和向量后，可获得线性方程分类解、超定系统的最小二乘解及残差，也可执行向量点积、叉积、范数、投影和夹角计算。

dsh-linalg README · dsh-linalg：Linear algebra toolbox for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`): matrix multiply, determinant, inverse, trace, transpose, reduced row echelon form, rank, integer matrix powers, a linear system solver that classifies unique / infinitely many / no solutions, a symmetric eigen-decomposition with measured residuals, matrix factorizations (LU with partial pivoting, thin QR, Cholesky) with measured reconstruction residuals, a least-squares solver for overdetermined systems, and vector operations (dot / cross / norm / projection / angle).
dsh-linalg README · dsh-linalg：Zero runtime dependencies, pure local arithmetic — no network, no processes, no eval.

dsh-linalg README · Why：Language models frequently make arithmetic errors on matrix multiplication, determinants, inverses and linear systems. This plugin hands those computations to exact local code with Gaussian elimination and partial pivoting, so results are deterministic and correct to 10 decimal places.

dsh-linalg README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:TYEclipse/dsh-linalg
```

Replace `web` with your profile name. (Requires `pnpm` on your PATH.)

dsh-linalg README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `matrix_multiply` | Multiply two matrices A·B with dimension checking |
| `matrix_compute` | One operation per call: `transpose`, `determinant`, `inverse`, `trace`, `rref`, `rank`, `power` (integer exponent) |
| `matrix_decompose` | One factorization per call: `lu` (P·A = L·U, singular flagged), `qr` (thin A = Q·R, R diagonal positive) or `cholesky` (A = L·Lᵀ, symmetric positive definite only) — each with a measured reconstruction residual |
| `matrix_eigen` | Eigen-decomposition of a real symmetric matrix: all eigenvalues (descending) + unit eigenvectors + measured residual |
| `least_squares` | Minimizer of ‖A·x − b‖ for overdetermined systems, plus the minimum residual norm and max ‖Aᵀ(A·x − b)‖ (rank-deficient / underdetermined input is an error) |
| `solve_linear` | Solve Ax = b; classifies unique / infinite (particular + nullspace basis + free-variable count) / no solution |
| `vector_ops` | `dot`, `cross` (3D), `norm`, `projection`, `angle` (degrees) |
dsh-linalg README · Tools：Input matrices are plain JSON arrays of arrays, e.g. `[[1, 2], [3, 4]]`. Maximum dimension is 20×20 by default (configurable).

dsh-linalg README · Examples：Determinant:

```
matrix_compute(matrix=[[2,1,1],[1,3,2],[1,0,0]], op="determinant")  →  -1
```

Inverse:

```
matrix_compute(matrix=[[4,7],[2,6]], op="inverse")
→ [[0.6,-0.7],[-0.2,0.4]]
```

Solve 2x+3y=8, x−y=1:

```
solve_linear(a=[[2,3],[1,-1]], b=[8,1])
→ unique solution: [2.2, 1.2]
```

Under-determined system (1 equation, 3 variables) reports the full parametric form:

dsh-linalg README · Examples：```
solve_linear(a=[[1,1,1],[1,2,3]], b=[6,14])
→ kind=infinite, particular=[-2,8,0], nullspaceBasis=[[1,-2,1]], freeVariableCount=1
```

Cross product:

```
vector_ops(op="cross", a=[1,2,3], b=[4,5,6])  →  [-3,6,-3]
```

Angle between [3,4] and the x-axis:

```
vector_ops(op="angle", a=[3,4], b=[4,0])  →  53.1301023542  (degrees)
```

Rank and integer powers:

dsh-linalg README · Examples：```
matrix_compute(matrix=[[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]], op="rank")  →  2
matrix_compute(matrix=[[1,1],[1,0]], op="power", exponent=20)
→ [[10946, 6765], [6765, 4181]]
```

`3.6180339887, 2.6180339887, 1.3819660113, 0.3819660113` — the closed form `2 − 2·cos(kπ/5)`.

dsh-linalg README · Numerical behaviour：- Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting (largest-magnitude pivot per column).
- All output numbers are rounded to 10 decimal places (configurable `roundPlaces`); values below 5e-12 are snapped to exactly 0, so `-0` never appears.
- Pivot tolerance is 1e-12: entries below that are treated as zero, so numerically singular matrices are reported as singular instead of producing garbage.
- Singular inverse requests fail cleanly with an error message; inconsistent systems return `kind: "none"` with the reducing row equation.
- `matrix_eigen` runs the cyclic Jacobi method in full double precision: every eigenvector is unit length, eigenvectors are signed so the leading non-zero component is positive, and the reply carries `maxResidual` = the largest `|A·v − λ·v|` entry actually measured. Non-square or non-symmetric input, and non-convergence, are reported as errors — never a guessed spectrum.
- `power` uses binary exponentiation; negative exponents invert first (and fail cleanly on singular input), exponents are limited to the integer range −64…64.
- `matrix_decompose` reports the residual it actually measured (`max |P·A − L·U|`, `max |A − Q·R|
